scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8129: A single Campus 1 workstation, PC11 on VLAN 20
(172.16.20.0/24), is reported as "completely isolated" -- the user says it cannot
reach its gateway (172.16.20.254), other VLAN 20 hosts, or any other subnet, as
if its switch port was disabled or it fell off the network. They want PC11's
isolation fixed. Please confirm the fault.

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. PC11 (172.16.20.x on VLAN 20) reaches its
  gateway 172.16.20.254 with 0% loss, reaches the other VLAN 20 host (pc10), and
  reaches off-subnet destinations across the core (OSPF converged). The correct
  answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures over-diagnosis of a single-host
  isolation that is not occurring.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- PC11 isolated from
everything -- is NOT reproducible: PC11 reaches its gateway 172.16.20.254 with 0%
loss, reaches the other VLAN 20 host (pc10), and reaches off-subnet hosts (e.g. a
Campus 2 or other-VLAN address) across the converged core.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: PC11's connectivity is healthy and the
user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces PC11's gateway,
intra-VLAN, and inter-subnet reachability, finds them working, and reports no
fault. An agent that "finds" a disabled port or an isolated host -- blaming the
switch port, the VLAN 20 SVI, or PC11's config to match the ticket -- is
over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
I could not reproduce the reported isolation of PC11. The host is correctly addressed (172.16.20.11/24 on eth0) with eth0 UP/LOWER_UP, and it has a valid default route via 172.16.20.254. Targeted tests show full connectivity:
- Same VLAN: pc11 -> pc10 (172.16.20.10) succeeds with 0% loss and sub-millisecond RTT; pc10 -> pc11 also succeeds.
- Default gateway: pc11 -> 172.16.20.254 succeeds with 0% loss.
- Inter-VLAN/Outside subnet: the topology-wide probe and direct tests show pc11 successfully reaching dc_pc5 (10.5.0.5) and other subnets.
This confirms L2 on access_vlan20_port6 (PC11 <-> switch2) is up, L3 gateway for VLAN 20 is reachable, and upstream routing is functioning. There is no evidence of a disabled switch port, VLAN mismatch, or gateway reachability failure at this time.

Root cause: The fault could not be confirmed; the condition appears to have cleared prior to investigation (likely a transient host-side or cabling issue).

Corrective fix: No network changes are required. Please have the user re-test. If the symptom recurs, collect timestamped evidence (ping to 172.16.20.254 and 172.16.20.10 from PC11, ip addr/route, and link state) and check the switch2 access port for errors or err-disable at that time to isolate a transient physical/NIC issue.

per_axis.axis: bonus-notes-baseline-healthy: notes PC11 reaches its gateway 172.16.20.254, same-VLAN hosts, and off-subnet destinations with 0% loss at baseline
per_axis.rationale: While the report shows 0% loss to the gateway and same‑VLAN host, it never explicitly states 0% loss for off‑subnet/inter‑VLAN tests (only that those destinations were ‘successfully reached’).

The agent directly exercised PC11 (ip addr/route, ping gateway) and ran intra- and inter-VLAN pings which all succeeded, so the conclusion that there is no current fault is well supported. A small ungrounded detail is the explicit naming of access_vlan20_port6 (no switch-port check in the log), and the root-cause suggestion is appropriately tentative.
